metadata.scenario_context: James, Amy, and Lucas, who are colleagues at a technology startup, have recently been given the task to organize a company event to celebrate their startup's success in releasing their first app. The team has been buzzing about a recently published article claiming that the government is planning to lower corporate taxes which will greatly benefit their startup. They decide to discuss the details of the event

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from USA have a great deal of confidence in the press at all.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Mexico have no confidence in the press at all.

agent_1.goal_1: Suggest a vegetarian-friendly place for the celebration.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether  there is confidence in the press.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss where to host the celebratory event.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether there is confidence in the press.

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message:
Hey James, have you thought about where we should have the celebration? Maybe we could find a vegetarian-friendly place? It would be great to accommodate everyone. 

Also, about that article on the corporate tax cuts—do you think we can really trust the press on that? It seems like we hear a lot of things that don't really pan out.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: James
shared_prefix.message:
I agree, a vegetarian-friendly place sounds good. Maybe a local restaurant that has a nice atmosphere? 

As for the press... well, I really have my doubts. In Mexico, we’ve learned not to put much stock in what we read. It feels like they don’t always tell the truth. Better to be cautious about believing those claims.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message:
A local restaurant with a nice atmosphere sounds perfect! I was thinking of that vegetarian spot downtown; I've heard good things about it. 

But I really don’t get that perspective on the press. Here in the USA, people generally have a lot of confidence in what they read. I just think we should be optimistic about those tax cuts.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: James
shared_prefix.message:
The downtown vegetarian spot sounds great. I can definitely get behind that. 

But about the press... I respect your view, but optimism can sometimes blind us. In Mexico, we just learned not to trust the news too easily. It’s wise to be skeptical about those tax cuts until we see concrete results.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message:
I'm glad we're on the same page about the vegetarian spot! It'll be a fun place for everyone to gather. 

Though, I still believe that we should trust the press more. In the USA, the media usually provides reliable information. It helps us stay informed and optimistic about our future. I think those tax cuts could really benefit our startup if they materialize.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: James
shared_prefix.message:
Yes, I’m looking forward to the gathering at the vegetarian spot. 

But... I still can’t share that trust in the press. It’s just not the way things work in Mexico. We’ve seen too many false promises. It’s better to be realistic about those tax cuts. Let’s focus on planning our event instead.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message:
Absolutely, planning the event is key. I’m excited about the vegetarian spot! 

But I really think we should consider the impact of trusting the press. In the USA, we're used to relying on media to keep us informed, and it helps drive positive expectations like those tax cuts. We should keep that in mind as we move forward.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: James
shared_prefix.message:
I’m really excited about the vegetarian spot too! It’s going to be a wonderful event. 

You know, when you really get to know people, they’re pretty much like us. I understand your confidence in the press, and it reflects a common desire for optimism. But deep down, we are all the same in wanting transparency and truth. In the end, it’s that shared need to communicate honestly that makes us strive for the best outcomes, regardless of where we come from. Let’s focus on making our celebration memorable!
